header_summary:
Luke Carriere's email outlines a draft policy aimed at standardizing enforcement policies across blockchain security services to address interoperability issues, particularly between products like Liquidium and Lendasat. The proposed standard involves various verification methods and ensures script-enforced conditions are included directly in the script, promoting broader integration without co-signer adjustments. Concerns addressed include serialization choices and verification technologies, with feedback sought on the structural placement of these policies within the blockchain framework. The draft for feedback is available at [Draft BIP](https://github.com/lukecarriere/bip-cosigner-spending-policies/blob/main/bip-cosigner-spending-policies.md).

A new dispute resolution method for blockchain-based games, detailed in a paper by AdamISZ, uses "venues" to verify actions within games like chess and blackjack played over Bitcoin's Lightning Network, enhancing scalability and efficiency. The system, vulnerable to collusion but designed without financial holding by venues, could extend to other complex contract disputes in decentralized systems. The full paper and its implementation are accessible [here](https://github.com/AdamISZ/ln-gap/blob/master/docs/paper/lngap-short.pdf) and on [GitHub](https://github.com/AdamISZ/ln-gap).

Developments in Bitcoin payments are advancing through the Intents protocol by Arkade, and other platforms like Kaleidoswap and Cassis, which employ HTLCs for multi-layer transactions. These initiatives offer various benefits such as instant settlement and enhanced privacy, with ongoing enhancements to address challenges in node communication and fund reclamation. Technical details and progress can be tracked on [GitHub](https://github.com/cassiscash/cassi).

recent_posts.title: LN-GAP : Lightning governed by arbitrary programs
recent_posts.summary:
- Recent blockchain advancements allow dispute resolution in smart contracts via "venues."- Venues act as impartial observers verifying game actions efficiently, minimizing blockchain load.
- Despite potential collusion risks, the system does not handle funds, reducing financial attacks.

recent_posts.title: Getting BIP54 past the finish line
recent_posts.summary:
- BIP 54 aims to fix critical security flaws in Bitcoin, including the timewarp attack.
- There are strong debates and a draft on eliminating 64-byte transactions in early 2025.
- Activation of BIP 54 is foreseen by mid-2027, requiring consensus and extensive testing.

recent_posts.title: Cassis, a new simple scheme for generic multi-layer multi-hop HTLC routing
recent_posts.summary:
- Bitcoin payment innovations include Arkade's Intents protocol and Kaleidoswap's HTLC network.
- Cassis introduces a chain of HTLCs for Bitcoin payments, enhancing flexibility and security.
- Ongoing improvements focus on communication standards and developing a reliable reputation system.

recent_posts.title: Anchoring an SPV light client on another chain: checkpoint trust, retargeting and reorg handling
recent_posts.summary: - The initial stateless verification model was discarded due to manipulation risks.  - An alternative suggests using a historical `bits` value with updates every four years.  - Another approach involves a canonical header chain track, simplifying block validation.

recent_posts.title: Disclosure: DoS vulnerabilities fixed in Eclair v0.14.1
recent_posts.summary: - The Phoenix wallet is not impacted by recent vulnerabilities in certain nodes.  - ACINQ preemptively patched potential security issues in Eclair months ago.  - Regular updates and maintenance are crucial for secure digital transactions.

active_posts.title: DropKick ⚽️ - A minimal commit/reveal PQ rescue protocol
active_posts.summary:
- DropKick aids Bitcoin users by securing assets using a blockchain commitment protocol.
- It employs a simple system that compares favorably with Dryja’s Lifeboat in terms of complexity.
- The protocol enables usage of third-party aggregators, enhancing flexibility for users.

active_posts.title: Flame: confidential transactions with Bitcoin proof-of-burn consensus
active_posts.summary:
- The Flame project uses a proof-of-burn mechanism for a decentralized Bitcoin side chain.
- It integrates privacy technologies like Bulletproofs and Ristretto for secure transactions.
- Scheduled for January 2027, Flame aims to mirror Bitcoin's security model and impact economics.

active_posts.title: RE BIP 300: 26% censoring attack
active_posts.summary:
- Attackers may manipulate Bitcoin Improvement Proposal 300 scores via ALARM messages.
- Proposed changes prohibit downvoting to uphold the 51% honest majority assumption.
- These adjustments aim to enhance security and fairness in Bitcoin transaction verification.

active_posts.title: PQC output type discussion
active_posts.summary:
- The email discusses integrating a P2TRv2 output type to enhance Bitcoin against quantum threats.
- It also proposes a long-term P2MR-based migration strategy for post-quantum readiness.
- Differing views on timing for ECC disabling are debated, focusing on security and autonomy.

active_posts.title: Shielded Bitcoin: Private Transfers on the Bitcoin L1
active_posts.summary:
- Shielded Bitcoin enhances Bitcoin transaction privacy using security vaults and PIPEs protocol.
- It enables private transfer validations via encrypted notes and zero-knowledge proofs.
- The system avoids altering Bitcoin's core rules and does not need a separate blockchain.

active_posts.title: What does "post-quantum" actually mean for a Bitcoin L2 when settlement still happens on a non-PQ L1?
active_posts.summary:
- Developing a Post-Quantum State-Channel on Bitcoin highlights blockchain's security issues.
- 'Peg-out' and 'peg-in' processes differ in handling post-quantum security challenges.
- Broader implications exist for BitVM-based bridges and similar blockchain integrations.

today_in_history_posts.title: Relaxing minimum non-witness transaction size policy restriction
today_in_history_posts.summary:
- A proposal suggests easing Bitcoin's non-witness byte policy from 85 to 65.
- The adjustment would facilitate smaller Bitcoin transactions with less required padding.
- Feedback on the proposal is sought; details and alternatives are on GitHub.

today_in_history_posts.title: Watchtower-Free Lightning Channels For Casual Users
today_in_history_posts.summary:
- Bastien and John discussed improvements on Lightning protocol's liquidity movement.
- They suggested protocol changes, including pre-signed splice transactions for efficiency.
- Their email exchanges and proposals are detailed in GitHub Pull Request 863.
